A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniversalRAG by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA evaluations, routing and granularity analyses, out-of-domain experiments, and qualitative results in the main text and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v3 reports original QA evaluations, cross-modal ablations, retrieval measurements, latency experiments, and additional analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v1 selects one of six routing categories and retrieves from a single corpus. v3 introduces multi-label selection of modality–granularity pairs, adds table retrieval, and jointly uses multiple sources. Its trained router uses binary cross-entropy and thresholded sigmoid outputs. Majority-voting ensembling is also added alongside the existing confidence-based fallback.

E1.justification: v3 adds text–table reasoning through HybridQA and image-containing queries through MRAG-Bench and InfoSeek. WebQA expands from single-image retrieval to text–image evidence. Out-of-domain coverage replaces LaRA's long academic/novel documents with 2WikiMultiHopQA's Wikipedia reasoning setting. SQuAD remains present, although its experimental role changes.

E2.justification: The main comparisons replace v1's InternVideo2-based Unified baseline with UniRAG, GME, PEcore, and VLM2Vec-V2, and add TableRAG and all-corpus MultiRAG. Existing fixed-modality methods retain their identities despite RAG suffixes. Random disappears from the detailed main and out-of-domain result tables but remains in v3 Table 5.

E3.justification: Generation backbones, router configurations, and retrieval encoders change substantially. Reported sample pools also change, including NQ from 1,000 to 2,000 queries and LVBench from 1,376 to 777; SQuAD moves from training/testing to out-of-domain testing. Video segmentation changes from fixed-duration to scene-based clips. New experiments introduce retrieval-recall metrics, corpus-size latency measurements, and additional granularity settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds cross-modal ablations, retrieval-modality and recall diagnostics, corpus-size latency analysis, five-encoder embedding visualizations, and routing failure cases. It extends granularity tests to four levels and revises router-size and ensemble analyses. Conversely, v1's generator-size sweep, confusion matrices, and per-dataset routing-count table are removed. Several earlier case-study questions are retained with updated evidence.

E5.justification: v1 does not specify a repeated-run count. v3 Appendix A.3 explicitly states that results come from a single run because of computational limits. This is newly disclosed run information, not evidence that run counts decreased. Neither version supplies uncertainty intervals, seed lists, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main and out-of-domain result grids are extensively replaced under changed models and settings, preventing direct version-to-version performance comparisons. New results include HybridQA EM of 11.05 with cross-modal versus 9.60 with unimodal retrieval for Qwen3-VL-2B routing (v3 Table 2), plus retrieval and latency measurements. v3 internally disagrees on GPT-5's in-domain average: 39.26 in Table 1 versus 41.68 in Table 5.

T1.justification: v1 provides framework equations without propositions or proofs. v3 Section 2.2 and Appendix C introduce three propositions, formal assumptions, and proofs concerning modality bias, adaptive granularity, and retrieval complexity, alongside set-valued routing definitions. These are substantive theoretical additions, although Appendix C.3's logarithmic-search limit does not establish its claimed strict asymptotic speedup.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from selecting one suitable corpus per query to jointly retrieving complementary evidence from multiple modality–granularity pairs, including tables. v3 also promotes theoretical justification and retrieval efficiency as contributions. The original modality-gap motivation and claims of superior average QA performance remain, with the main benchmark claim expanding from eight to ten datasets.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of complementary cross-modal evidence, irrelevant-modality noise, nonmonotonic granularity gains, and retrieval scalability. Its new Limitations section discusses noisy automatic routing labels and missing fine-granularity annotations. Appendix F explains routing ambiguities and why disagreement with proxy labels need not harm answers. The earlier trained-versus-training-free generalization trade-off is retained.

D1.justification: v3 specifies classifier implementation, LoRA rank 32, routing threshold 0.8, GPU/VRAM information, PySceneDetect clipping, and frame-embedding averaging for baselines lacking video support. It also documents new corpus construction, score aggregation, and expanded routing prompts. Conversely, v1's explicit top-1 generation-context and best-validation-checkpoint selection statements are omitted.

R1.justification: v3 broadens research positioning through discussion and citations covering UniRAG, PEcore, VLM2Vec-V2, E5-V, MM-Embed, and the text-conversion alternative RAG-Anything, alongside new benchmark and model literature. GME was already cited in v1; its updated title and publication metadata are not a newly introduced work.

P1.justification: The introduction, preliminaries, method description, and related-work prose are substantially rewritten and condensed. Separate experimental setup and results sections become a combined Section 3; metric descriptions move to Appendix A.3. The appendices are reorganized around theory, additional experiments, embedding analysis, and qualitative results, with new limitations and ethics sections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to depict cross-modal and granularity routing and moves to the first page. The main results display changes from three generator panels to one, with other generators presented in Appendix Table 8. Average-score plots are redesigned, while new distribution, latency, embedding, cross-modal, and failure-case displays accompany removal of the earlier confusion matrices and generator-size plot.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's single-source experiments and single unified-embedding baseline, v3 provides more informative cross-modal ablations, broader evaluated competitors, and useful implementation and failure-analysis detail. These yield a limited net quality improvement. The gains are tempered by new reliability problems: conflicting GPT-5 averages in Tables 1 and 5, and an unsupported strict asymptotic speedup conclusion in Appendix C.3.
